description: Declarative per-column validation in the Svelte 5 data grid. Each column gets a validate function returning true or a message; the grid runs it for every rendered cell, including values already in the data on load, and paints invalid cells red with the message as a tooltip. The check re-runs live as you edit, so fixing a value clears the red and breaking a good one lights it up, and the value is never rolled back.
keywords: svelte 5 data grid invalid cell highlight

faq.question: How do I add validation to a column?
faq.answer: Add validate: (params) => message | true to the column definition. Return true when the value is fine and a string explaining the problem otherwise; the grid uses the string as the tooltip on the red cell.

faq.question: Does it catch bad data that was already there?
faq.answer: Yes. The hook runs for every rendered cell, so rows that arrive invalid are flagged the moment the grid mounts, which a commit-time validator cannot do.

faq.question: Does validation block the edit?
faq.answer: No. What you type is what is stored; the cell just stays red until the value passes. For a hard reject, roll the value back in onCellValueChange instead.
